risks.statement: False readiness can start oversized or ambiguous work.
risks.trigger: Any codex-ready issue fails a readiness rule.
risks.response: Remove the label and repair the issue before execution.

risks.statement: A persistence or identity slice can start before its provider foundation is verified.
risks.trigger: A data-isolation or identity-dependent issue is made ready without its provider dependency complete.
risks.response: Add the dependency and execute the provider foundation first.

risks.statement: Linear release membership can drift from the delivery manifest.
risks.trigger: A live release count or issue assignment differs from the generated release plan.
risks.response: Fail the drift gate, repair the assignment, and read back all affected releases.

risks.statement: Only one human member is available for ownership and approval.
risks.trigger: A second active human workspace member becomes available.
risks.response: Until then, require CI and a separate Codex review before named Blake Rowley release or checkpoint approval; when another human joins, require a distinct human reviewer, split issue owner and reviewer, and recalibrate capacity.

risks.statement: Scheduled Linear drift enforcement depends on a repository secret.
risks.trigger: The scheduled workflow runs without LINEAR_API_KEY.
risks.response: Fail closed and configure the read-only key before treating scheduled drift as operational.

risks.statement: Default-to-R0 classification can pull later-release behavior and its dependency chain into the first release.
risks.trigger: R0 contains behavior that is not required for the defined one-buyer, one-seller defensible-evaluation journey.
risks.response: Use an explicit R0 journey allowlist and keep enhanced behavior in its owning later release unless a smaller source-bound R0 slice exists.

risks.statement: Truncated Linear list responses can make incomplete issue text look authoritative in the delivery snapshot.
risks.trigger: A listed description contains a truncation marker or omits executable fields present only in the full issue.
risks.response: Fetch the full issue before qualification and fail readiness when full text cannot be obtained.

risks.statement: External provider access can dominate calendar delivery while remaining invisible in active-work throughput.
risks.trigger: The next dependency-safe issue lacks required provider identity, credentials, or environment configuration.
risks.response: Withhold the calendar date, report external wait separately, and do not start dependent work before provider proof passes.

risks.statement: Unresolved release or dependency ownership defaults can hide a required prerequisite or falsely signal readiness.
risks.trigger: A DEC-REL-* validation trigger fires, new source or runtime evidence changes an ownership default, or affected work is proposed as codex-ready.
risks.response: Block readiness, revalidate the pinned source and runtime path, update the decision, dependency graph, and release policy, then regenerate and synchronize before execution.

risks.statement: A first production release without healthy provider predecessors and a live pre-mutation known-good canary can leave no proved rollback path.
risks.trigger: Production staging or promotion is attempted while any DEC-PROD-001 prerequisite is absent.
risks.response: Fail before provider mutation, provision or separately approve the bootstrap, and prove the live rollback anchor before customer traffic or domain promotion; historical receipts alone never authorize release.

risks.statement: Waiting for invited-human release proof while candidate Convex code is live can expose unproved behavior or strand a release after the runner exits.
risks.trigger: A release attempts to collect customer or operational proof without the isolated candidate target and durable coordinator required by DEC-PROD-002.
risks.response: Block promotion, restore and prove the known-good Convex release, and collect proof only after the isolated candidate, authenticated durable handoff, expiry compensation, and single-use finalizer are operational.

risks.statement: The first Vercel production activation has no predecessor and cannot provide atomic cross-project rollback.
risks.trigger: Baseline activation stops after one or more applications receive traffic but before all three exact candidates are proved live and healthy.
risks.response: Stop new mutations, re-read every project and domain, retain the immutable stage receipt, mark recovery_required, and resume only the remaining exact candidates from that receipt. Never label the partial state rolled back; strict rollback requires a separately provisioned healthy maintenance predecessor for every project.

risks.statement: A later GitHub rerun can change the latest workflow-run record and invalidate an otherwise immutable successful baseline artifact.
risks.trigger: Baseline provenance is read from the mutable run endpoint instead of the exact successful attempt endpoint.
risks.response: Bind the artifact, run, SHA, and conclusion to the attempt-specific GitHub readback and reject any proof that depends on the latest mutable attempt.

risks.statement: A reason-only bootstrap can mint recovery authority without proving first genesis or an expired anchor.
risks.trigger: Bootstrap is requested without an exhaustive, receipt-bound inventory of prior production and bootstrap anchors.
risks.response: Allow only machine-proven initial genesis or exact expired-anchor recovery, keep the authority non-promotable, and require the DEC-PROD-002 single-use finalizer before mutation.

risks.statement: Cancellation during a Vercel mutation can outlive the runner grace period and lose recovery evidence.
risks.trigger: A baseline provider command remains active after a cancellation signal or any pinned production domain is not proved on the promoted deployment.
risks.response: Terminate promptly, persist recovery_required with traffic unknown, and reconcile only through the same immutable receipt; promotion passes only when every pinned production domain is assigned.

risks.statement: Co-locating Vercel and Convex write credentials gives one process unnecessary cross-provider mutation authority.
risks.trigger: A job or process receives both provider credential classes before the durable phase coordinator is operational.
risks.response: Fail closed and split stage, mutation, promotion, and compensation into receipt-bound provider-specific jobs before enabling production mutation.

risks.statement: Artifact retention, deletion, or workflow identity changes can erase the GitHub evidence needed to distinguish first genesis from recovery.
risks.trigger: A production authority approaches expiry, an authority artifact or run is deleted, or an authority-producing workflow is renamed, copied, or removed.
risks.response: Keep every artifact-derived anchor non-promotable and block provider mutation until a protected non-expiring genesis sentinel and single-use finalizer preserve authority history independently of Actions retention.
